correctness.rationale: An integral dual functional has vertex values \(f_i=u_i+w u_{i+1}\), and the coefficient extrema force width at least \((w-1)(\max u-\min u)\). Alternation uniquely attains \(w-1\) for even \(n\). At odd \(n\), binary nonconstant normals have width at least \(w\), with equality exactly if they avoid cyclic \(00\) or \(11\). The only nonbinary candidate (\(w=2\) and coefficient range two) would force transitions \(01,02,11,20,21\), and no nonconstant odd cyclic walk uses these. This proves the classification. The Lucas count is a bijection to nonempty independent sets of \(C_n\). A packaged exact-integer bounded checker verified 306,168 comparisons and 352 minima, supplementary only.

value.rationale: Lattice width is a canonical geometric invariant measuring integer hyperplane layers. The result completely classifies optimal dual directions of a natural graph-defined circulant simplex family in every dimension and discovers a sharp parity discontinuity: one unoriented minimizing normal for even order versus \(L_n-1\) (exponentially many) for odd order. The independent-set correspondence organizes the entire minimizer geometry and is not a routine substitution into either motivating paper.
